doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Show of Shows television and the snake mishap
summary: Band as house band on a live coast-to-coast TV show, with a turban, fake snake and collapsing music stand.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well tell me stories about the band.
No, no. We played out in Hollywood on the “Show of Shows.” It was an hour and a half coast to coast T.V. show. We were the house band. And we did “Moonlight on the © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Ganges,” the number that almost killed my career in music when I auditioned for the band. But they came out and they put a turban on me so I looked like a Hindu, and they put a turban on Eddie Sauter and Eddie’s conducting, and at the rehearsal they had a string tied to an overhead teaser and on the bottom of the string was a fake snake, and when I played “Ganges” somebody would wiggle the string and you’d see the fake snake going like this. This was live television, 1954. So come the show, somebody untied the string and they’re weaving this string, or they thought they untied the string but they didn’t. It was still tied to my music stand and they started wiggling this snake in front of me, and a stage hand started pulling up the scenery, and my music stand went up and I thought I was sinking and I’m playing oboe like this, the string broke, the music came down and knocked over instruments. This was coast to coast television. Anyway.
That’s just one of the many stories that we had.
